A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, principal contributions, and experiments. Text, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original GFlowNet training experiments on hypergrid and permutation environments in Section 4, Table 1, and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported sampling errors, trajectory lengths, and normalizing-constant estimates.

M1.justification: The DB/SDB loss variants, proposed state-flow regularization in Equation 12, policy parameterizations, and implemented training procedures are retained. Revisions to the RL appendix concern mathematical definitions and proofs.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 7×7 and 20×20×20×20 hypergrids and permutations of lengths 4, 8, and 20, using the same rewards and scenarios. Newly cited application domains are not new experiments.

E2.justification: Corresponding figures and Table 1 retain the same DB/SDB comparators and combinations of flow scale, regularization, and fixed or trainable backward policies. No newly cited method joins the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains the model sizes, optimizer settings, training budgets, metrics, and previously specified sampling windows. The added checkpoint-averaging and reward sample-count information documents existing evaluations without establishing a revised protocol or rerun.

E4.justification: The fixed-versus-trainable backward-policy comparisons, loss-scale analyses, unregularized trajectory-growth experiment, and regularization-strength sweep are retained, including Figures 4–6 in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 newly discloses averaging log Z estimates over the last 10 training checkpoints before computing the error, clarifying point-estimate aggregation. Table 1 retains means and standard deviations over three random seeds; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Table 1 values and uncertainties, all six numbered figures, and the reported experimental findings match. For example, the n=20 DB log-flow configuration with regularization 10^-5 retains fixed-point L1 error 0.017 ± 0.002 and mean trajectory length 7.55 ± 0.50.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1 explicitly adds graph finiteness. Appendix A.7 replaces the infinite-sum return definition with a stopped return and zero sink value; Lemma A.1 changes the zero-reward condition from one outgoing action to one incoming edge and adds finite expected length for optimal policies. Its proof is revised accordingly. Appendices A.1, A.4, and A.7 also clarify reasoning and correct formulas, including a state-flow factor and a missing logarithm. These are localized revisions within the retained framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about discrete non-acyclic GFlowNet theory, backward policies, flow regularization, loss scaling, and equivalence with entropy-regularized RL.

C2.justification: v2 makes the finite-graph applicability boundary explicit and qualifies the group-based motivation by acknowledging that acyclic constructions can sometimes generate group elements. Interpretations of the experimental accuracy–trajectory-length tradeoffs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly specifies the last-10-checkpoint averaging used for log Z error and that mean reward is computed over 10^4 samples. Existing implementation settings remain available. The same source-code link moves from Section 4 to the introduction.

R1.justification: v2 expands citations covering molecular generation, biological design, optimization, language models, and RL. It credits Deleu (2025) for mentioning constrained optimization for cyclic GFlowNets and adds or replaces mathematical references. The central positioning relative to Brunswic et al. remains intact; publication updates and duplicate-reference consolidation are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The introduction expands the group-generating example and RL motivation, and prose receives grammatical and explanatory edits. A Discussion heading labels existing observations, and an Impact Statement and updated conference/funding text are added. The overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Table 1's caption receives light editing, and surrounding text and equations reflow across pages. The six numbered figures, explanatory graph diagrams, and table structure retain their visual content without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: Explicit finiteness and termination conditions, revised reasoning, and corrected equations make the existing theory more precise. The added condition qualifies Lemma A.1, while the principal contributions remain intact. Appendix C.3's calculation details improve reproducibility, and expanded context improves readability. These are useful but limited gains; the empirical evidence is unchanged.
